item.title: Third Post
item.description:
Failure Wiki

Reading about the post office scandal which happened in the UK due to technical glitches caused by software called ‘Horizon’, developed by the Japanese company Fujitsu, led to one of the most devastating institutional failures.

This scandal made me realise how comfort or ignorance of something can lead to disastrous outcomes. Unfortunately, over a thousand sub-postmasters were wrongfully prosecuted and some even comitted the suicide. People placing their comfort in the assumption that technology is always accurate is vastly the reason why these events happened in the first place.

item.title: Second Post
item.description:
Optimization

Optimization models are genuinely so cool. While solving problems and thinking this must be the answers now, you figure that you were so wrong.

Well, I did not except it to be straightforward either. I quickly understood that there’s much more about how you think rather than what you know. Almost all the time, my instinct led me in the wrong direction because I overllooked things and structure of the problem.

item.title: First Post
item.description:
Github&Hugo

I think the setting up the whole reflection blog website was fun. It was moderately challenging and I feel having a reflection blog where you update about life is so introspective and also gives you with something to look upon later.

Also, I had to help my groupmates quite a lot. I think this is because they have never troubleshooted before and tried reading documentation to figure out solutions.However, they got it when I pinpointed the issue. Most of them either didn’t update their baseURL or mention the theme specifically in hugo.toml file. What I found interesting was showing them how to approach the problem rather than just giving solution. By guiding them to read through the documentation and find relevant content for deploying the site, then they were atleast able to put their head to it and make progress.
